record.field: International Standard Classification of Education (ISCED 2011). A comprehensive framework for organizing education programmes and qualifications by applying uniform and internationally agreed definitions to facilitate comparisons of education systems across countries. Adopted by the UNESCO General Conference in November 2011.

Education designed to support early development in preparation for participation in school and society. Programmes at this level are typically designed for children below the age of entry into primary education (ISCED level 1). Includes early childhood educational development (ages 0-2) and pre-primary education (ages 3 to start of primary).

Programmes typically designed to provide students with fundamental skills in reading, writing and mathematics and to establish a solid foundation for learning. Entry age is typically between 5-7 years old, and duration is usually 4-7 years (most commonly 6 years).

Programmes building on primary education, typically designed to lay the foundation for lifelong learning and human development. Often more subject-oriented than primary education, with more specialized teachers. Typically 2-5 years duration, often ending after 8-9 years of education from the start of primary.

Programmes typically designed to complete secondary education in preparation for tertiary education or to provide skills relevant to employment, or both. More varied, specialized and in-depth instruction than lower secondary. Typically 2-5 years duration, often ending after 12-13 years of education from the start of primary.

Programmes providing learning experiences that build on secondary education and prepare for labour market entry or tertiary education. Content is not complex enough to be regarded as tertiary education although it is clearly post-secondary. Duration typically ranges from 6 months to 2-3 years.

Programmes designed to provide participants with professional knowledge, skills and competencies. Typically practically-based, occupationally-specific, and prepare students to enter the labour market. May also provide a pathway to other tertiary education programmes. Duration typically 2-3 years full-time equivalent.

Programmes designed to provide intermediate academic or professional knowledge, skills and competencies leading to a first tertiary degree or equivalent qualification. Duration typically 3-4 years full-time equivalent (may be up to 6 years for professional programmes like medicine).

Programmes designed to provide advanced academic or professional knowledge, skills and competencies leading to a second tertiary degree or equivalent qualification. May include a substantial research component. Duration typically 1-4 years full-time equivalent following a bachelor's degree.

Programmes designed primarily to lead to an advanced research qualification, usually concluding with the submission and defence of a thesis or dissertation of publishable quality. Typically requires a minimum of 3 years full-time equivalent, with total duration commonly 5-8 years.
Never attended or completed any formal education programme. May include informal learning or non-formal education not classified within the ISCED framework.
Education level not stated, unknown, or not elsewhere classified.
